title: Why Does Knocked-Sideways Uranus Have 21-Year Winters?
description:
Why Knocked-Sideways Uranus Has 21-Year Winters

At the North Pole of Uranus, the seventh planet in orbit around our Sun, what would you see when the Sun sinks below the horizon? A single winter night that lasts 21 Earth years. While Earth spins at a 23.44-degree tilt, Uranus is tipped at 97.77 degrees — more than four times Earth's tilt, and nearly at a right angle to its orbit — rolling around the Sun on its side like a ball. How did an entire giant planet get knocked onto its side?

Sources: NASA Science, Uranus Facts — seventh planet from the Sun, 97.77-degree axial tilt nearly at a right angle to its orbit, rolling around the Sun like a ball, and a 21-year-long dark winter (https://science.nasa.gov/uranus/facts/) · NASA NSSDCA, Uranus Fact Sheet — obliquity to orbit 97.77 degrees on Uranus versus 23.44 degrees on Earth (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/uranusfact.html).

Pictures: NASA/JPL Voyager 2 (PIA18182, PIA01391, PIA00032, PIA00346, PIA00143), NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope NIRCam (weic2310a), NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope (PIA01280, PIA02963), and NASA Apollo 17 (PIA18033) alongside original animated explainers, with AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech (Voyager 2, PIA18182, PIA01391, PIA00032, PIA00346, PIA00143); NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Joseph DePasquale (STScI) (weic2310a); NASA/JPL/STScI (Hubble Space Telescope, PIA01280, PIA02963); NASA/JSC (Apollo 17, PIA18033).
